svg.aria-label: How to write ï ë ü: 3 letters, ï, ë, ü, one after another
svg.title: Writing ï ë ü
svg.desc: 3 letters written one after another: ï, ë, ü (latin). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/LatinPrint-Subset.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ï: By analogy with the cited ü, not separately sourced: the stem of the i after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/i (assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/i/metadata.json, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only), then the two dots last, as UJIpenchars2's native Spanish writers draw the marks of ü (UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) <https://github.com/Medien-Treibhaus/grundschrift-app-source/blob/f6dbd807adbb3fc2f94207fe578def439f6e9c49/assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/i/metadata.json>; ë: By analogy with the cited ü, not separately sourced: the e after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/e (assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/e/metadata.json, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only), then the two dots last, as UJIpenchars2's native Spanish writers draw the marks of ü (UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) <https://github.com/Medien-Treibhaus/grundschrift-app-source/blob/f6dbd807adbb3fc2f94207fe578def439f6e9c49/assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/e/metadata.json>; ü: UJIpenchars2 (F. Prat, M. J. Castro, D. Llorens, A. Marzal and J. M. Vilar), UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, class ü: 120 tablet pen traces by 60 native Spanish writers (CC BY 4.0); the u after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/u (commit f6dbd80) <https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/177/uji+pen+characters+version+2>. Source notes on variation: ï: ORDER BY ANALOGY, NOT SEPARATELY SOURCED. No source reachable here records how ï is written: the Grundschrift-App has no letter with this mark, and UJIpenchars2 holds Spanish characters only. So its order is drawn by analogy with the cited ü. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) finds the two dots of ü drawn last in 119 of its 120 traces, and the left dot first in 116 of the 118 where both are found. ï is therefore the stem of the Grundschrift-App's i, whose dot the two dots replace (level kleinbuchstaben/i, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only), then the two dots after it, the left dot first, as ü's are. Only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are claimed, and only by analogy; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the ï of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. ë: ORDER BY ANALOGY, NOT SEPARATELY SOURCED. No source reachable here records how ë is written: the Grundschrift-App has no letter with this mark, and UJIpenchars2 holds Spanish characters only. So its order is drawn by analogy with the cited ü. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) finds the two dots of ü drawn last in 119 of its 120 traces, and the left dot first in 116 of the 118 where both are found. ë is therefore the Grundschrift-App's e (level kleinbuchstaben/e, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only), then the two dots after it, the left dot first, as ü's are. Only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are claimed, and only by analogy; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the ë of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. ü: UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of ü, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. 117 are three strokes. The two dots come last in 119 of the 120, and the left dot comes first in 116 of the 118 where both are found. The u is the Grundschrift-App's u (level kleinbuchstaben/u, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only). Only counts and shares are cited; no trace is copied, and the path is fitted to the ü of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer.
